analysis.summary: Brazil enter as heavy favourites after winning Group C with seven points, led by Vinicius Jr. (four goals in three matches) and Matheus Cunha (three goals). Japan finished second in a competitive Group F unbeaten but carry a significant injury burden — captain Wataru Endo (foot surgery), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), and Takumi Minamino (ACL) are all absent — stripping them of key creators and their most dangerous wide threat. Brazil are the stronger side on paper and should advance, but Japan have demonstrated counter-attacking ability and beat Brazil 3-2 in a friendly in October 2025, making a Japanese goal highly plausible.
analysis.home_form: Brazil won Group C with 7 points (W2 D1): 1-1 draw with Morocco (Vinicius equaliser), 3-0 win over Haiti (Raphinha injury, Cunha brace), 3-0 win over Scotland (Vinicius brace, Cunha). Vinicius Jr. has 4 tournament goals; Cunha 3. Neymar came off the bench vs Scotland. Pre-tournament losses of Rodrygo (ACL), Militao (hamstring), Estevao, and Wesley weakened the squad depth; Raphinha suffered a hamstring tear vs Haiti and is expected to miss the Round of 32.
analysis.away_form: Japan finished second in Group F with 5 points (W1 D2): 2-2 draw with Netherlands (Kamada, Doan goals), 4-0 win over Tunisia (Ueda brace, Kamada goal), 1-1 draw with Sweden. Kamada and Ueda are the top scorers with two goals each. Japan were unbeaten but the 4-0 margin against Tunisia flatters their form; the Netherlands and Sweden draws both required late resilience.
analysis.h2h: Brazil lead the all-time head-to-head 11 wins to 1, with two draws, scoring 37 goals to Japan's 8 across 14 meetings. The sole WC meeting was at the 2006 group stage, where Brazil won 4-1 (Japan led briefly). Japan's only win came in a 3-2 friendly in October 2025, a remarkable comeback after trailing 2-0 at half-time, with goals from Minamino, Nakamura, and Ueda — though Minamino is now absent through injury.
injuries_news: Brazil OUT: Raphinha (hamstring tear sustained vs Haiti, ruled out for Round of 32, quarterfinal return possible), Rodrygo (torn ACL, season-ending pre-tournament), Militao (hamstring surgery, pre-tournament), Estevao (hamstring, pre-tournament), Wesley (pre-tournament).
Brazil CONCERN: Casemiro was substituted at half-time vs Morocco; status for this match is unconfirmed.
Japan OUT (pre-tournament): Wataru Endo (captain, foot surgery), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Takumi Minamino (ACL).
Japan CONCERN: Ko Itakura (defensive fitness monitored), Takehiro Tomiyasu (recently recalled to squad after lengthy absence, fitness unconfirmed).
Yellow card slate wiped clean after group stage — no carry-over suspensions into Round of 32 under 2026 FIFA rules.
key_factors: Japan's triple injury crisis removes Endo (midfield engine and captain), Mitoma (main wide threat), and Minamino (the scorer in the 2025 comeback win) — their creative ceiling in this match is significantly lower than in that friendly.

Vinicius Jr. is in peak tournament form with four goals in three matches; without Raphinha on the opposite flank, the burden falls heavily on him and Cunha, but that combination was already highly effective vs Scotland.
NRG Stadium's retractable roof is expected to be closed with air conditioning active for the 17:00 UTC (12:00 local) kickoff, neutralising Houston's extreme June heat and humidity for both sides.
Brazil had five days' rest after their June 24 Scotland match; Japan had four days after their June 25 Sweden draw — rest differential is minimal.
Japan's counter-attacking structure (Kubo, Doan, Kamada, Ueda) can punish any high defensive line Brazil adopt, as demonstrated in the 2025 friendly comeback.

This is a ROUND_OF_32 knockout fixture — the h2h market settles on the result after extra time. A 90-minute draw leads to extra time and potentially penalties, where Brazil's experience and depth provide additional edge.
